title: Small Habits That Last

article.heading: REPEATABLE ACTIONS
article.paragraph: A habit becomes easier to keep when the action is simple enough to repeat every day.

article.heading: LONG-TERM CHANGE
article.paragraph: Consistency matters more than intensity when we are building a lasting change.

article.heading: REPEATABLE ACTIONS
article.paragraph: The first step should be small enough that it does not depend on perfect motivation. Attaching a new action to an existing routine makes it easier to remember. Tracking a habit can provide useful information without turning the routine into a competition. Missing one day is a signal to adjust the plan, not a reason to abandon it. A flexible routine can survive changes in schedule, energy, and unexpected events. People are more likely to continue when progress is visible in a simple form. The purpose of a routine is to support a life, not to control every moment of it. Over time, repeated choices can become evidence that a person is capable of change.
